name: Covered Call Unwind (Buy-Write Close)
summary: The correct exit mechanic for any share-plus-short-option unit: close the short option and the shares as a single combination order so cover is never broken mid-flight.

legs.strike_rule: close the existing short call at any strike

max_profit: n/a - this is an exit mechanic, it realizes the unit's existing P/L
max_loss: n/a - realizes existing P/L; the risk is execution slippage and momentary uncovered exposure if legged
when_to_use: Whenever a covered call, buy-write, covered strangle or collar unit is being closed for any reason: profit target, stop, thesis change, expiration guard, or portfolio rebalance.
entry_rules: ALWAYS submit as a single multi-leg order (sell stock + buy to close call). Alpaca supports multi-leg equity+option combos; if the combo is rejected, the fallback ORDER OF OPERATIONS is: buy to close the option FIRST, confirm the fill, THEN sell the shares. Never the reverse - selling shares first leaves a naked short call, which the account is not approved for and which the broker may auto-liquidate.
Price the unwind at the net mid, then walk the limit by 5% of the spread every 15 seconds up to 3 attempts.
Verify final share count and option position after the fill; any residual is a reconciliation alarm.
management_rules: If the combo cannot fill within 3 attempts, split: close the option at market, then work the share sale.
Log the realized unit P/L against the tracked basis (entry debit minus cumulative credits) rather than against the raw share price.
exit_rules: Must complete before 15:30 ET on expiration day for any ITM short leg.

If a partial fill occurs (option closed, shares unsold), the remaining shares are simply an unhedged long - acceptable. If the reverse occurs (shares sold, option open), it is a naked short call - close it IMMEDIATELY at market, regardless of price.
assignment_risk: The entire purpose of this mechanic is to eliminate the assignment/naked-exposure window that legging creates. The dangerous state is shares-sold-option-open; the system must treat that as a P0 alarm with an immediate market close.
buying_power: Frees the shares and any reserved cash.
liquidity_needs: Combo markets are thinner than single legs; be willing to fall back to sequential closing in the correct order.
common_mistakes: Selling the shares first; walking the limit too slowly near the close; not reconciling the ledger after a partial fill.
zero_dte_notes: On 0DTE, do not attempt combo pricing near the close - just buy to close the option at market before 15:30 ET and handle the shares separately.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
